activities.title: Appearance and hardness of metals
activities.summary: Observe iron, copper, aluminium, magnesium; clean with sandpaper; compare lustre and cut with knife.

activities.title: Malleability, ductility, sonority
activities.summary: Beat metals with hammer; draw wires; tap metals — note malleability, ductility, and sonorous sound.

activities.title: Heat and electrical conductivity
activities.summary: Heat metal wire with pin in wax; test metals in electric circuit with bulb.

activities.title: Non-metal properties
activities.summary: Test carbon (coal), sulphur, iodine for lustre, malleability, conductivity — compare with metals.

activities.title: Burning metals
activities.summary: Burn magnesium ribbon, copper wire, and aluminium foil in air; observe flame and residue.

activities.title: Metals with water
activities.summary: Add Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Fe, Cu, to cold/hot water or steam; compare reactions.

activities.title: Displacement reactions
activities.summary: Place metal strips in salt solutions (CuSO₄, ZnSO₄, FeSO₄, AgNO₃); observe colour changes and deposits.

activities.title: Burning sulphur
activities.summary: Burn sulphur powder; test gas with litmus paper; note acidic oxide formation.

activities.title: Reactions with oxygen
activities.summary: Burn samples of metals and non-metals in air; classify oxides as basic/acidic/neutral.

activities.title: Ionic compound properties
activities.summary: Test NaCl, MgCl₂, etc. for melting point, solubility, and conductivity solid vs solution.

activities.title: Extraction of metals
activities.summary: Discuss reduction of metal oxides with carbon; electrolytic reduction for high-reactivity metals.

activities.title: Electrolytic refining
activities.summary: Study diagram of electrolytic refining of copper — anode, cathode, electrolyte.

activities.title: Corrosion conditions
activities.summary: Iron nails in test tubes A (air+water), B (boiled water+oil), C (dry air/CaCl₂); compare rusting.

exercise_mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs will give displacement reactions?
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Cu is more reactive than Ag; Cu + 2AgNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag.

exercise_mcqs.question: Which of the following methods is suitable for preventing an iron frying pan from rusting?
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Grease, paint, and galvanisation (zinc coating) all prevent rust by blocking air and moisture.

exercise_mcqs.question: An element reacts with oxygen to give a compound with a high melting point. This compound is also soluble in water. The element is likely to be
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Calcium forms basic oxide CaO (high mp) which gives soluble Ca(OH)₂ with water.

exercise_mcqs.question: Food cans are coated with tin and not with zinc because
options: zinc has a higher melting point than tin
zinc is more reactive than tin
zinc is less reactive than tin
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than tin; it could react with food acids — tin is less reactive and safer as coating.

intext_samples.question: Metals in their pure state have a shining surface. This property is called
intext_samples.explanation: The shining surface of pure metals is called metallic lustre.

intext_samples.question: Metals that can be beaten into thin sheets are called
intext_samples.explanation: Malleability is the property of being beaten into thin sheets.

intext_samples.question: Ionic compounds are formed by
options: transfer of electrons from metal to non-metal
intext_samples.explanation: Metal atoms lose electrons; non-metals gain them — ionic bond forms.

intext_samples.question: Which metal can displace copper from CuSO₄ solution?
intext_samples.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the reactivity series and displaces Cu from CuSO₄.

intext_samples.question: Galvanisation protects iron because zinc
options: forms a barrier and sacrificial coating
reacts with iron to form alloy
intext_samples.explanation: Zinc coats iron and corrodes preferentially, protecting the iron underneath.
